title: Al-'Alaq: the first words
hook: read, in the name of your Lord who created you from a clinging clot, who taught by the pen (96:1–5)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Al-Qadr, the night the Qur'an was first revealed. Your line was peace until dawn. Did you end the night with a quiet minute in the dark? Day one hundred eighty-one.

A cave, high on a mountain outside Mecca, just big enough for one person to sit. A man of about forty climbs up there often, to be alone, to think, to turn toward God, with food his wife Khadijah has packed. One night, according to Muslim tradition in the month of Ramadan, someone else is in the cave. Yesterday we heard about that night. Today we hear the words that were actually spoken in it: the first words of the Qur'an to be revealed. Today: Al-'Alaq, the first words.
screen: `A CAVE ON A MOUNTAIN.` → `SOMEONE ELSE IS IN THE CAVE.` → `THE FIRST WORDS REVEALED.`

segments.voice: The story is told by Aisha in the opening pages of Sahih al-Bukhari. The angel Jibril came to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in the cave of Hira and said one word: iqra'. Read, or recite. The Prophet answered: I am not a reader. The angel pressed him tight, until he could bear no more, and said again: read. Three times. And then came these words, in Pickthall's translation: Read: In the name of thy Lord who createth, Createth man from a clot. Read: And thy Lord is the Most Bounteous, Who teacheth by the pen, Teacheth man that which he knew not. 'Alaq, the word the surah is named for, means something that clings. Pickthall says clot; many translators today prefer a clinging thing, and scholars discuss the range. The point is the contrast: a human begins as something tiny and clinging, and is taught what he did not know. And notice the pen. The first revelation to a man who said I am not a reader is about reading and writing. Knowledge, from the very first line, is a gift from Allah. The Prophet came down the mountain shaking and went home to Khadijah and said: cover me, cover me. She wrapped him up, listened, and told him: Allah would never disgrace you. You keep ties with family, you help the weak, you honor guests, you stand by people in hardship. The first person to believe him was the person who knew him best. Taught by the pen.
screen: `IQRA' — READ.` · `I AM NOT A READER.` · `A CLINGING THING, TAUGHT WHAT IT KNEW NOT.` · `COVER ME — AND KHADIJAH DID.` · then, large: `TAUGHT BY THE PEN.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: write one line by hand. Find a pen and any paper, a receipt, the back of an envelope. If you can't right now, trace the letters with a finger on your palm. Write one thing you learned this week that you didn't know before. Go slowly. Feel the pen move. Then sit with it. Somebody taught you that, or something did. Notice where knowledge comes from. The bell holds the time.
Al-'Alaq. The clinging thing, the name of Surah ninety-six, whose first five verses were the first of the Qur'an revealed. Today's word.
Your line: taught by the pen. Write one line by hand today, on paper, and keep it. Let it remind you that everything you know, you were taught. Day one hundred eighty-one.

howItsDone: Muslims learn the story of the first revelation in the cave of Hira as part of the Prophet's life; the opening verses of Surah al-'Alaq are recited in the prayers and often quoted to honor learning.

fork.setup: your husband comes down the mountain shaking, saying something happened in the cave. you're Khadijah. what do you do?
options: tell him to stop climbing up there
cover him, listen, and remind him of the good he does
fork.reveal: she covered him and said Allah would never disgrace him: he kept family ties, helped the weak, honored guests (Bukhari).

original.note: Arabic: read, or recite; the first word revealed, the same root as Qur'an.

trapdoor: what you thought: a surah about a blood clot.
what it means: the first words revealed: read, in the name of the Lord who created you from something clinging and taught by the pen.
what a scholar hears: Bukhari 3 (Aisha's account); iqra' shares the root q-r-' with Qur'an; 'alaq translated clot, leech-like or clinging thing; most scholars hold 96:1–5 was first.

sources.quoted: Read: In the name of thy Lord who createth, Createth man from a clot. Read: And thy Lord is the Most Bounteous, Who teacheth by the pen, Teacheth man that which he knew not.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3 (the first revelation, told by Aisha)

notes: Please confirm the exact Pickthall wording of 96:1–5.
Bukhari 3 cited from memory; Khadijah's words paraphrased.
'In the month of Ramadan' follows tradition linking 96:1–5 with the Night of Power (97:1, 2:185); confirm framing.
Translations of 'alaq vary (clot, clinging substance, leech-like); the script says 'scholars discuss the range'.
